newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market in suspense over possible hike.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market in suspense over possible hike.

text.p: Trade on the Dutch money market was quiet on Monday morning as market players were in suspense over a possible hike in the special advances rate and the secured loans rate at 1500 GMT.
"It's waiting for the yes or no, that's the main story today," one trader said, adding the zest might come back once the market knew where things were standing.
"For many parties, there's no big point in doing a deal right now, if they can possibly do it at a higher rate tomorrow," he said.
All money market rates were slightly higher than on Friday, with overnight money mostly traded at between 2.94 and 3.06 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said the market priced in a hike in the special advances rate, which sets the tone for money rates, but they did not agree over a possible raise in the secured loans.
"Most banks count on a hike in special advances of at least 0.10 percent, while corporates, public utility companies, communities are waiting to see what will happen," one said.
He added there was a tiny possibility that the secured loans rate, which sets the floor for rates, would be hiked as well.
"The gap between the two rates is just too big," he said.
Another trader said a hike in the special advances rate could be as big as 0.20 or 0.30 percent.

"I have trouble believing anyone who's telling me it won't be hiked. They're (the central bank) watching the guilder/mark very closely and the short (four-days) special advances pact certainly has its reasons," he said.
He added that the central bank had no choice but to raise its secured loans rate as well if it moved the other rate.
The Dutch central bank hiked its special advances rate by 20 basis points to 2.70 percent on February 27.
The secured loans rate, the equivalent of Germany's official discount rate, has been pegged at 2.00 percent since April 1996.
The hike in the special advances rate did not strengthen the guilder versus the mark.
The guilder was trading at 112.634 per 100 marks around 1120 GMT, continuing to weaken from Friday's level of 112.605.
